pool.text: The urban centre officially became the capital city of the Portuguese territory.
King Denis I founded the first Portuguese university in the urban centre.
King Juan I of Castille besieged the city during an ongoing crisis.
Manuel I decreed that all resident Jewish inhabitants must convert to Christianity.
An anti-Semitic riot by Old Christians led to numerous deaths of New Christians.
Damião de Góis wrote and published a description of the municipality.
A military coup d'état ended the republic and established the Estado Novo regime.
The longest suspension bridge in Europe, the 25 de Abril Bridge, was inaugurated.
The Estádio da Luz held the European Cup Final.
ISCTE - Lisbon University Institute was founded to provide academic degrees.
The New University of Lisbon was founded as another public university.
The Carnation Revolution ended the right-wing regime and reformed the country.
Lisbon joined the Union of Ibero-American Capital Cities since its founding.
Lisbon became part of the Union of Capital Cities of Portuguese Language.
A fire destroyed many historic buildings in the Chiado district of the capital.
The municipality was designated as the European Capital of Culture for the year.
The urban settlement organised the Expo '98 world exposition event.
The Vasco da Gama Bridge was opened as the longest European bridge.
The European Union signed an agreement to revitalise the economy in the capital.
The capital hosted the annual MTV European Music Awards ceremony event.
